To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we introduce a deep generativemodel for representation learning of protein sequences that explicitly represents the evolutionary history of the sequences; (2) our model outperforms existing models on the task of reconstructing ancestral sequences; (3) we show that the model is able to capture important properties of the evolutionary process, and we discuss how the model can be extended to genomic-scale data

a deep generative tree-structured Ornsteiin-Uhlenbeck variatonal autoencoder is a promising approach for representation learning of protein sequences that outperforms the state-of-the-art in the task of ancestral protein sequence reconstruction.
a tree-structured prior can improve sequence reconstruction and that a tree-structure is a suitable prior for protein sequences.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how to represent the evolutionary process of biological sequences in a probabilistic model.

the development of a new class of deep generative models that can explicitly capture evolutionary information and thus improve the performance of existing methods for protein sequence representation learning.
the development of a deep generative sequence model that can be trained on genomic data and that explicitly represents the evolutionary history of the data.

the model is able to reconstruct ancestral proteins in a reasonable way.
the proposed model has the potential to significantly improve representation learning of genomic data.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our model is able to capture the evolutionary process in a more explicit way and therefore is better able to learn representations of sequences that are more useful for downstream tasks.

the model is able to learn a representation of protein sequences that is useful for ancestral sequence reconstruction and that the explicit representation is a key component for achieving good results.

the proposed method is capable of generating ancestral sequences of protein families that are more realistic and more similar to the observed ones compared to the ones generated using a standard variational autoencoder model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
deep generative models can benefit from the inclusion of a suitable evolutionary prior.
deep generative models for biological sequences can benefit from the explicit representation of the evolutionary process.
the explicit use of a phylogenetic prior in a deep generative framework is a promising approach to representation learning of biological sequence data.
